title: Telework and Technostress: A Systematic Review of Risk and Protective Factors for Workers’ Well-Being
abstract: The consolidation of telework has introduced digital demands that may increase technostress and threaten employees’ psychological well-being and sustainable career development. Grounded in Conservation of Resources theory, this systematic review examined psychosocial risk factors associated with technostress in telework, protective individual and organizational resources, and the contribution of digital psychological support interventions. Following PRISMA guidelines, Scopus, Web of Science, and PubMed were searched between June and August 2025 for peer-reviewed empirical studies published from 2022 to 2025 involving remote or hybrid adult employees. Fourteen of 556 identified records met the PICOS-based eligibility criteria. Methodological quality was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools. Digital overload, technological complexity, work intensification, and blurred work–life boundaries were associated with poorer psychological and work outcomes. Digital self-efficacy, adaptability, proactive personality, supportive leadership, trust, and communication emerged as protective resources. Digital psychological support interventions may reduce emotional strain and strengthen resources for sustainable careers.
